prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [反例] 组标题长于子列 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Merged cells: "城市" spans 1 col × 2 row; "空气质量指数（AQI）月度平均值" spans 3 col × 1 row; "说明" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "城市" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 27px
  col 2: header "空气质量指数（AQI）月度平均值 › 一月" · longest unbreakable word 17px · one-line width 27px
  col 3: header "空气质量指数（AQI）月度平均值 › 二月" · longest unbreakable word 17px · one-line width 27px
  col 4: header "空气质量指数（AQI）月度平均值 › 三月" · longest unbreakable word 17px · one-line width 27px
  col 5: header "说明" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 306px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"比较北京、上海和广州前三个月的空气质量指数月平均值，并结合说明理解变化。","reading":"读者可按行比较同一城市的月度变化，也可沿单月列比较不同城市；说明文字为数值提供背景。","groups":["第一列标识城市，是每行数值和说明的共同参照。","第二至第四列分别是一月、二月和三月的同类指标，应保持相同宽度，方便横向和纵向比较。","第五列是文字说明，与前三个月的数值共同构成一行。"],"keep_intact":["城市名称、月份名称和各项数值应各自保持完整。","AQI 缩写应保持完整。"],"may_wrap":["跨三列的长组标题可在中文词语边界换行。","说明文字可自然换行；较长说明形成的行高也可容纳组标题以外的数据行内容。"]}

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored.
